documents.annotated: Much of the [[s1|ImageJ]] ecosystem, including the [[s2|ImageJ2]] platform and the plug-ins designed for it, can be run in a headless mode without visible [[s3|ImageJ]] components. All headless routines are discovered by the search service within [[s4|ImageJ2]] and integrated directly into [[s5|napari]] within a new [[s6|napari]] widget (Fig. 1a). By presenting these routines via this mechanism, [[s7|napari-imagej]] minimizes both the display footprint and the amount of [[s8|Java]] and [[s9|ImageJ]] terminology exposed to the user while maintaining comparable performance to usage from within the [[s10|ImageJ]] user interface (see for benchmarking analysis). Third-party plug-ins and scripts written for the [[s11|ImageJ2]] platform are also automatically exposed in the search results, maximizing extensibility.

documents.annotated: We develop [[s1|CodeT5+]], a new family of open code large language models for code understanding and generation tasks (see Fig. 1 for an overview and more architecture/pretraining details in Fig. 2 and Fig. 3). documents.annotated: Our environment was provisioned under [[s1|Python]] [[v1|3.10.12]] on a workstation running [[s2|macOS]] [[v2|13.5]], with an earlier configuration evaluated under [[s3|Python]] [[v3|3.8.10]] and a legacy check under [[s4|Python]] [[v4|2.7.18]] for backward compatibility. All dependencies were installed through the [[s5|pip]] package installer and recorded with the [[s6|pip]] freeze utility into a requirements.txt manifest; an equivalent environment was later rebuilt under [[s7|conda]] [[v7|23.3.1]] and exported as environment.yml. documents.review_notes: requirements.txt and environment.yml are files, not software. pip freeze is a command of pip, not a separate tool. Versions 3.9.7/3.11.4 refer to Python but the exact occurrence owner is ambiguous, so ownership scoring masks those two versions (not their detection).
